newsitem.title: USA: Atlas Air sees "flattish" Q1 - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Atlas Air sees "flattish" Q1 - analysts.

text.p: Atlas Air Inc on Tuesday told analysts in a conference call that it expected its first-quarter results to show little change from the same period last year, analysts said.

"There were some comments in the conference call that created some uncertainty about the first quarter. They said the first quarter would probably be flattish compared to last year," said Michael Shonstrom of Neidiger Tucker Bruner.
Atlas Air, which provides cargo services for major international airlines, also told analysts that certain maintenance expenses were running higher than expected.
Atlas officials did not return calls seeking comment.
Atlas was one most active Nasdaq issues on Tuesday, dropping 9-3/4 to 24-3/4 by late afternoon.
Earlier on Tuesday, Atlas posted fourth-quarter earnings of $0.60 a share on operating revenues of $104.7 million, compared with earnings of $0.43 on operating revenues of $56.1 million last year.

Shonstrom said he planned to reduce his first-quarter earnings estimate to about $0.30 a share from an earlier forecast of $0.40. The consensus estimate on Wall Street is $0.49 a share, according to First Call.
In the first quarter last year, Atlas earned $0.32 a share on operating revenues of $58.6 million.

Analysts said they expected Atlas to post stronger results starting in the second quarter of 1997. The company's revenues should grow with the completion of pending aircraft acquisitions, analysts said.
In a prepared statement, Atlas President Mickey Foret said the Golden, Colo.-based company would take delivery of a minimum of five additional aircraft this year, increasing its fleet to 22 aircraft.

"We will be expending significant effort and resources to successfully integrate these aircraft and to reduce our overall unit costs. Indeed, one of our major focuses in 1997 will be to achieve further cost efficiencies in our flight and maintenance areas and to avoid the growing pains normally associated with growth of this magnitude," Foret said.
Atlas also said it was in talks to acquire additional planes beginning in 1998.
Separately, Atlas said it received commitments to increase the size of its revolving aircraft acquisition facility to $275 million from $175 million.
